extracted.intended_audience: hospital administrators, hospital finance officers, Medicare providers, health policy analysts, state health agencies, and stakeholders submitting comments on CMS IPPS/LTCH PPS rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Impact analysis and methodological explanation for CMS's proposed FY2027 changes to the Inpatient Prospective Payment System (IPPS) and LTCH PPS, including modeling assumptions, population inclusion/exclusion, and payment component calculations used to estimate year-over-year payment impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significant regulatory action / RIA requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 3(f) of Executive Order 12866 defines a “significant regulatory action” and requires a regulatory impact analysis (RIA) for actions that meet those criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Executive Order 12866's section 3(f) lists four prongs that make a regulatory action significant: (1) annual economic effect of $100 million or more or materially adverse effects on economy, environment, public health/safety, or governments/communities; (2) creates serious inconsistency or interferes with another agency's plans; (3) materially alters budgetary impact of entitlements/grants/user fees/loans or recipients' rights/obligations; or (4) raises novel legal or policy issues arising out of mandates or President's priorities. When significant under 3(f)(1), an RIA must be prepared; OMB's OIRA review and CMS's RIA present estimated costs and benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary objectives of IPPS and LTCH PPS
rubrics_metrics.description: The primary objective of the IPPS and the LTCH PPS is to create incentives for hospitals to operate efficiently and minimize unnecessary costs while ensuring payments adequately compensate hospitals for delivering necessary care to Medicare beneficiaries and preserving the Medicare Hospital Insurance Trust Fund.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy choices should further efficiency, adequate compensation, access to high-quality care, preservation of Medicare HI Trust Fund, and avoid or minimize unintended adverse consequences. Rationale for each policy is provided in the section where it is discussed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations and caveats of quantitative impact analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantitative estimates present projected effects holding many variables constant and using the best available data, but generally do not adjust for future changes in admissions, lengths of stay, case mix, Medicare population, or incentive-driven behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimates of individual proposed policy changes are made by estimating payments per case while holding other payment policies constant. CMS notes difficulty in precisely quantifying impacts due to interdependent payment components, potential miscategorizations from different data sources, and reliance on experience or limited data where model inputs are unavailable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hospitals included and excluded from IPPS analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Prospective payment systems encompass most general short-term acute care hospitals participating in Medicare; some hospitals are excluded from IPPS analysis due to special payment methodologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excluded: Indian Health Service hospitals (26 in database), hospitals in Maryland (AHEAD Model), hospitals outside 50 states/DC/PR (e.g., territories) paid on reasonable cost subject to rate-of-increase ceiling. CAHs (approx. 1,385) are paid on reasonable costs and analyzed separately. IPPS-excluded units include IPFs, IRFs, LTCHs, RNHCIs, children's hospitals, cancer hospitals, extended neoplastic disease care hospitals, and certain short-term acute care hospitals in territories; their payment impacts are not included in IPPS proposed rule (LTCH impacts discussed separately).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data sources and baseline methodology for payment simulation model
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of specific data files and baseline parameters for simulation: FY2025 MedPAR, Provider-Specific File (PSF), most recent cost reports for categorization, and a FY2026 baseline model with defined payment parameters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The simulation begins with a FY2026 baseline using: FY2026 national adjusted operating standardized amount; FY2026 MS-DRG GROUPER (Version 43); FY2026 CBSA designations from 2020 Census; FY2026 wage index and labor/nonlabor share percentages; FY2026 uncompensated care payments; FY2026 outlier payments (CMS used an estimate of 6.0% of total operating MS-DRG and outlier payments derived from FY2025 MedPAR). For proposed changes lacking data, CMS predicts impacts based on experience or limited data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modeling approach: isolate individual policy effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Effects of individual proposed policy changes are estimated by simulating payments per case while generally holding all other payment policies constant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This permits estimating the impact of a single change on payments per case; however, CMS notes interactions among payment components can make precise attribution difficult, and some proposed changes cannot be modeled due to lack of data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outlier payments target and outlier offset
rubrics_metrics.description: Statute requires outlier payments to be projected between 5% and 6% of total operating DRG payments plus outlier payments; CMS uses a 5.1% target and applies an outlier offset factor to the standardized amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS used an outlier offset factor of 0.949 (reflecting 5.1% target), as in FY2026. CMS's payment simulation showed estimated outlier payments for FY2026 were ~0.9 percentage points higher than the 5.1% target; returning to the target produces a net decrease in payments (example: overall hospitals experienced a 0.7% decrease attributable primarily to the -0.9% change in outlier payments when returning to 5.1%).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicable percentage increase (hospital update) and quality/EHR adjustments
rubrics_metrics.description: Each year CMS updates the national standardized amount by an 'applicable percentage increase' (market basket less productivity adjustment); for FY2027 proposed applicable percentage increase = 3.2% market basket − 0.8% productivity = 2.4%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are four possible applicable percentage increases depending on whether a hospital submits quality data under §1886(b)(3)(B)(viii) and whether it is a meaningful EHR user under §1886(b)(3)(B)(ix). CMS models reduced updates for hospitals failing to submit quality data and/or not meaningful EHR users. Section 1886(b)(3)(B)(iv) makes SCHs and MDHs' hospital-specific rate updates equal to the same update factor as other IPPS hospitals, subject to the same quality/EHR adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of MDH special payment status expiration
rubrics_metrics.description: MDH (low-volume Medicare-dependent hospital) special payment status provided a nonbudget neutral blended payment; expiration affects payments for qualifying hospitals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under current law MDH status was extended through 12/31/2026; expiration for discharges on/after 1/1/2027 causes affected hospitals to lose blended payment (higher of Federal rate or Federal rate +75% of the difference between Federal rate and hospital-specific rate) and receive only the Federal rate, leading CMS to estimate a ~0.1% overall decrease in IPPS payments and an estimated ~$110 million decrease for the subset that would have received blended payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uncompensated Care Payments (UCP) calculation and modeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed changes to uncompensated care payments and supplemental payments are quantified and their effect on total operating IPPS payments estimated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For FY2027 CMS proposes total uncompensated care payments and proposed supplemental payments of approximately $8.5 billion; CMS estimates the proposed UCP changes would result in a 0.2% decrease in total operating IPPS payments relative to FY2026. A more detailed analysis is referenced (section I.G.2).

rubrics_metrics.name: MS-DRG reclassifications, relative weights, and recalibration budget neutrality
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS annually updates MS-DRG classifications and relative weights to reflect treatment patterns and technology; applies recalibration budget neutrality and a 10% cap on relative weight reductions to ensure overall budget neutrality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For FY2027 CMS calculated proposed MS-DRG relative weights using FY2025 MedPAR grouped to proposed Version 44 GROUPER. CMS applied a recalibration budget neutrality factor to account for the changes and a permanent 10-percent cap on reduction in a MS-DRG's relative weight with an associated recalibration cap budget neutrality factor. With application of these factors, Column 5 (All Hospitals) showed a 0.0% net change due to MS-DRG/weight changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wage index update and labor-related share
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual update to wage data used to calculate the wage index is required by statute; for FY2027 CMS proposes using cost reporting periods beginning on/after Oct 1, 2022 and before Oct 1, 2023 and a proposed labor-related share of 66.0%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Column 6 reflects changes when moving from FY2026 wage index to proposed FY2027 wage index based on updated data and a labor-related share of 66.0%, holding other parameters constant (e.g., Version 44 GROUPER). CMS uses proposed wage data updates and applies wage index budget neutrality adjustments as described elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wage index budget neutrality adjustment
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS applies a wage index budget neutrality factor to the national standardized amount to ensure overall payments under the updated wage index are budget neutral (subject to statutory exceptions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For FY2027 CMS calculated a proposed wage index budget neutrality factor to make payments budget neutral without regard to the lower share (62%) applied to hospitals with a wage index ≤ 1.0. The factor is summarized among proposed FY2027 budget neutrality factors in the Addendum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic reclassifications and reclassification budget neutrality
rubrics_metrics.description: MGCRB reclassifications, urban-to-rural reclassifications under §1886(d)(8)(E), and Lugar status redesignations affect wage index values and must be applied with a reclassification budget neutrality adjustment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because section 1886(d)(8)(D) requires geographic reclassification effects to be budget neutral, CMS applies a reclassification budget neutrality adjustment to offset the fiscal effect of these reclassifications. Table 2 in the Addendum lists reclassifications used for FY2027 modeling; readers referred to section III.E for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rural floor and rural floor budget neutrality
rubrics_metrics.description: The rural floor requires an urban hospital's wage index not be less than the wage index applicable to rural hospitals in the same state; application of the rural floor is accompanied by a uniform budget neutrality adjustment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS applies a rural floor budget neutrality adjustment reducing all IPPS hospitals' wage indexes to offset the fiscal effects of imposing the rural floor; details in section II.A.4.e. of the Addendum and summary table of FY2027 budget neutrality factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-budget-neutral wage index provisions: imputed floor, frontier state minimum, out-migration adjustment
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain wage index provisions are non-budget neutral and are applied in Column 6: (a) imputed floor for certain all-urban States under §1886(d)(3)(E)(iv); (b) minimum post-reclassified wage index of 1.00 for hospitals in 'frontier States' under §1886(d)(3)(E)(iii); (c) proposed out-migration adjustment under §1886(d)(13).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These provisions are applied in combination with other wage index changes; they are treated as non-budget-neutral adjustments in CMS's combined effect calculations for FY2027.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categorization and presentation of impact results
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS groups hospitals into categories to illustrate varying impacts: geographic (urban/rural, bed-size, census division), payment classifications (SCHs, MDHs, reclassifications), teaching/DSH status, ownership and Medicare/Medicaid utilization, and reclassification status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables present overall impact and subgroups (urban/rural; bed-size within urban/rural; census divisions; payment classifications post-reclassification; GME/IME and DSH combinations; rural special payment groups; ownership and percent Medicare/Medicaid inpatient days; reclassification subgroupings including MGCRB decisions and Lugar hospitals). This enables illustrating heterogeneity of proposed changes across hospital types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of combined (Column 7) effects and interactive considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Column 7 presents estimated percent change in payments per discharge from FY2026 to FY2027 reflecting the combined effects of all proposed changes, acknowledging interactive effects between factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS reports overall average increase (~1.2% for all hospitals) and differential effects by urban/rural (urban 1.2%, rural 0.8%), noting drivers (outlier adjustment, hospital update, uncompensated care changes) and that interactive effects and relative weight changes lead to larger increases for hospitals treating more complex cases and decreases for those treating less complex cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: New medical service and technology add-on payment calculation and modeling assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Under §412.88(a)(2), the new technology add-on payment for each case is limited to the lesser of: (1) 65% of the costs of the new technology (75% for QIDPs, LPAD-approved products, or certain gene therapies when used for SCD); or (2) 65% of the amount by which costs of the case exceed the standard MS-DRG payment for the case (75% for the same exceptions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because predicting actual add-on payments per case is difficult, CMS's estimates are based on the applicant's cost estimates at application time and assume every qualifying claim would receive the maximum add-on payment. For FY2027 CMS proposes to continue 41 previously approved new technology add-on payments and discusses applications (47 received; 17 withdrawn/not eligible). Add-on payments are not required to be budget neutral.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative pathway criteria for new technology add-on payments
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the alternative pathway, technologies with QIDP designation, FDA LPAD approval, or Breakthrough Device designation are considered not substantially similar to existing technologies and do not need to demonstrate substantial clinical improvement, but must meet other criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such technologies must still be within the 2- to 3-year newness period and meet the statutory cost criterion. CMS proposed to approve 22 alternative pathway applications for FY2027 and estimated potential payments (approx. $589 million based on preliminary applicant-provided information), excluding one technology lacking cost/volume information.
